title: Semisimple rational modules restricted to a dense abstract subgroup
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field] [def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $G$ be a smooth affine finite-type $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme] [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $\Gamma\subseteq G(k)$ be a Zariski dense abstract subgroup. A rational representation on a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space $M$ is a group-scheme homomorphism $\rho:G\to\operatorname{GL}(M)$, where $\operatorname{GL}(M)(R)=\operatorname{Aut}_R(M\otimes_k R)$ for a commutative $k$-algebra $R$. A rational subrepresentation is a $k$-subspace preserved after every such extension; simple means nonzero with no nonzero proper rational subrepresentation. For an abstract $\Gamma$-representation, a subrepresentation is a $k$-subspace preserved by each $\gamma\in\Gamma$, and simple has the analogous meaning. If $M$ is a finite direct sum of simple rational $G$-subrepresentations, then its restriction to $\Gamma$ is a finite direct sum of simple abstract $\Gamma$-subrepresentations. Moreover every $\Gamma$-invariant subspace $N\subseteq M$ has a $\Gamma$-invariant complement $C$, so that $M=N\oplus C$. In particular, every surjective $\Gamma$-equivariant $k$-linear map $q:M\twoheadrightarrow V$ to an abstract $\Gamma$-representation has a $\Gamma$-equivariant $k$-linear section $s:V\to M$ with $q\circ s=\mathrm{id}_V$. Zero spaces and disconnected groups are allowed; no characteristic-zero or finiteness hypothesis on $\Gamma$ is imposed.

source.place: Proposition 1.10, printed pp.9--10; Proposition 4.3 and Corollary 4.4, printed p.85 (schematically dense subgroup detects rational subspaces); Proposition 4.17, printed p.90 (complements in a sum of simple representations); proof of Lemma 13.6, printed p.256, invoking 4.4 and choosing stable sections.

proof.text: For any $\Gamma$-stable $k$-subspace $W\subseteq M$, the stabilizer $\operatorname{Stab}_{\operatorname{GL}(M)}(W)$ is Zariski closed by [lem-wf-stabilizer-density] (only its first assertion is used). Its inverse image under $\rho$ is a closed subset of $G$ containing every point of $\Gamma$. Density makes that closed subset all of $G$. Consequently every $g\in G(k)$ preserves $W$. The action is invertible and $g^{-1}$ also preserves $W$, so $\rho_k(g)W=W$. If $M=0$, the unique subspace is already preserved and the conclusion of this argument is immediate.

source.place: Proposition 4.3 and Corollary 4.4, printed p.85: closed stabilizer and dense-subset argument.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-group-rational-point-subspace-test] to $G$, $M$, and $W$. Its condition (i) was proved in step 1, and its hypotheses hold because $k$ is algebraically closed and $G$ is smooth, affine and finite type. Its condition (ii) says exactly that $W$ is a rational subrepresentation, including preservation over nonreduced $k$-algebras. Conversely a rational subrepresentation is $\Gamma$-stable by evaluating at $k$ and restricting to $\Gamma$. Thus the rational $G$-subspaces and abstract $\Gamma$-subspaces of $M$ coincide.

source.place: Corollaries 4.4--4.5, printed p.85; the existing rational-point test supplies the all-algebra conclusion.

proof.text: Write the given decomposition $M=\bigoplus_{i=1}^r S_i$ into nonzero simple rational subrepresentations. Each $S_i$ is $\Gamma$-stable. A $\Gamma$-stable subspace $T\subseteq S_i$ is also a $\Gamma$-stable subspace of $M$, hence rationally $G$-stable by steps 1--2. Viewed inside $S_i$, it is a rational subrepresentation: tensor inclusions over the field are injective, and the action on $S_i$ is the restriction of that on $M$. Rational simplicity gives $T=0$ or $T=S_i$. Thus each restricted $S_i$ is simple, and the same finite direct sum proves the first assertion. For $M=0$ use the empty sum.

source.place: Corollary 4.4, printed p.85, applied as in the proof of Lemma 13.6, printed p.256.

proof.text: Use the ring $R=k[\Gamma]$ of finite formal sums $\sum_\gamma a_\gamma[\gamma]$, with $[\gamma][\delta]=[\gamma\delta]$, acting on $M$ by $\left(\sum a_\gamma[\gamma]\right)m=\sum a_\gamma\rho_k(\gamma)m$. Its submodules are exactly the $\Gamma$-stable $k$-subspaces: one direction uses the elements $a[1]$ and $[\gamma]$, and the other follows by closure under finite sums. The same correspondence holds in each $S_i$, so step 3 makes each $S_i$ a simple $R$-submodule. Every element of $M$ is a finite sum of elements of these simple submodules. Apply [lem-sfb-module-socle-complements] to this unital ring and module. For each $\Gamma$-stable $N$ it gives an $R$-submodule $C$ with $M=N\oplus C$. By the displayed correspondence, $C$ is a $\Gamma$-stable $k$-subspace, as required.

source.place: Proposition 4.17, printed p.90; its general ring-module form is the existing Mathlib leaf.

proof.text: For a surjective equivariant $k$-linear map $q:M\to V$, put $N=\ker q$. It is $\Gamma$-stable since $q(\gamma n)=\gamma q(n)=0$. Choose $C$ by step 4. The restriction $q|_C:C\to V$ is injective because $C\cap\ker q=0$, and surjective because if $q(m)=v$ and $m=n+c$, then $q(c)=v$. Let $s$ be its inverse followed by $C\hookrightarrow M$. Uniqueness of the preimage in $C$ gives $s(av+bw)=as(v)+bs(w)$ and $s(\gamma v)=\gamma s(v)$, since $C$ is stable. Hence $s$ is $k$-linear and equivariant, and $q\circ s=\mathrm{id}_V$. If $M=0$, surjectivity forces $V=0$ and the same construction gives the unique section.

source.place: Proposition 4.17, printed p.90, and the stable isomorphic lifts used in the proof of Lemma 13.6, printed p.256; explicit kernel-complement argument.

proof_origin.place: Corollary 4.4 (p.85), Proposition 4.17 (p.90), and the simplicity and stable-lifting argument in Lemma 13.6 (p.256).
